name: Seedance 2.5
summary: Reference-rich storytelling with longer connected sequences.
specs: Up to 30 seconds • Native audio/video • Multimodal references
strengths: Large reference sets, scene planning and targeted edits support connected story beats.
weaknesses: New-release claims are vendor-reported; complex identity, contact and continuity still need review.
best: A 20-second product story using supplied people, location and sound references.
worst: Exact engineering demonstrations or a complete multi-minute film in one generation.

name: Seedance 2.0 / Fast / Mini
summary: A mature short-sequence option with several speed tiers.
specs: Up to 15 seconds on base model • Audio • Image/video/audio references
strengths: Reference-guided motion and sound suit short branded sequences; lighter variants offer iteration choices.
weaknesses: Limits differ by provider and variant. ByteDance acknowledges text, multi-subject identity and audio artifacts.
best: Short character ads with reference assets; test Fast/Mini for drafts before final generation.
worst: Small readable text, flawless hand-object interaction or assuming Mini equals base quality.

name: Kling 3.0 / 3.0 Omni
summary: Multi-shot direction with synchronized multilingual audio.
specs: Up to 15 seconds • Native audio • Reference workflows vary by mode
strengths: Shot sequencing, character references and sound make it useful for narrative scenes. Omni adds broader multimodal control.
weaknesses: Standard and Omni are distinct workflows; access and options vary. References reduce rather than eliminate drift.
best: A dialogue-led social ad with several shots and a recurring character.
worst: Long uninterrupted scenes requiring exact physical continuity or guaranteed verbatim typography.

name: Kling 2.6 Motion Control
summary: Use a driving performance to animate an image.
specs: Image + motion reference • Motion-control workflow
strengths: Recorded movement gives more direct choreography than describing every gesture in text.
weaknesses: Output inherits limitations of the driving clip; occlusion and body proportions can complicate transfer.
best: A mascot copying a simple dance, gesture or presenter performance.
worst: A brand-new complex action sequence without a suitable motion reference.

name: Veo 3.1 / Fast
summary: General-purpose film shots with integrated sound.
specs: Text/image to video • Native audio • Reference and extension features depend on surface
strengths: A useful starting point for realistic scenes, dialogue and environmental sound; Fast supports iteration.
weaknesses: Short generation windows require editing longer stories; exact speech, object persistence and physics need checking.
best: A cinematic establishing shot, atmospheric B-roll or a short spoken scene.
worst: Long factual demonstrations or projects that cannot tolerate rerolls and sound correction.

name: Gemini Omni Flash
summary: Conversational creation and revision using mixed media.
specs: Text, image, video and audio context • Iterative editing
strengths: Changing an existing scene through conversation can preserve more context than restarting from scratch.
weaknesses: Editing scope and access depend on the product. Local changes can still alter unintended details.
best: Refine a clip's setting, styling or action while keeping the larger scene recognizable.
worst: Pixel-exact compositing or workflows requiring deterministic preservation of every untouched region.

name: Runway Gen-4.5
summary: Detailed shot direction in a production-oriented toolset.
specs: 2–10 seconds in documented web workflow • 720p • 24/25 fps
strengths: Camera choreography and prompt adherence support planned shots; pairs with Runway editing tools.
weaknesses: Native output in the cited workflow is 720p. Finishing and audio may require separate stages.
best: An art-directed hero shot with a clear subject, camera path and action.
worst: Native high-resolution delivery without finishing, or a one-click long dialogue scene.

name: Runway Gen-4 / Turbo
summary: Image-led motion for economical iteration.
specs: Image-to-video • Standard and faster Turbo tiers
strengths: A strong supplied frame anchors look and composition; Turbo is useful for trying several motion ideas.
weaknesses: Older generation; input image quality matters. Speed does not ensure the most faithful difficult action.
best: Animate approved campaign artwork or explore several camera moves before a final render.
worst: Text-only scene creation in this workflow or exact continuity across many independent clips.

name: Runway Aleph 2.0
summary: Transform existing footage through an editing workflow.
specs: Video editing • Edit Studio • Professional output options vary
strengths: Useful for changing environments, visual treatment and scene elements while starting from footage.
weaknesses: Generative edits are not deterministic masks; SDR outputs should not be mistaken for native HDR.
best: Restyle a shot or explore alternative set dressing without reshooting.
worst: Exact frame restoration, legally evidentiary footage or precise color-only corrections.

name: Runway Act-Two
summary: Transfer an actor's delivery to a character.
specs: Driving performance video + character image/video
strengths: Real performed timing, expression and gestures give intentional acting direction.
weaknesses: Requires a usable performance; multi-character scenes need separate shots and editing.
best: A stylized character delivering a recorded line or demonstrating a gesture.
worst: Unscripted crowd action, vehicle scenes or shots without a driving performance.

name: Luma Ray3.2 Modify
summary: Footage-guided transformation with keyframe control.
specs: Modify: video-to-video • Up to 20 seconds • Up to 16 keyframes • HDR/EXR workflows
strengths: Existing movement plus keyframes gives directors explicit anchors; production formats support finishing.
weaknesses: Modify requires source footage and follows its duration. It is a different task from unconstrained text generation.
best: Replace a filmed environment or evolve a scene's appearance across planned beats.
worst: Creating a whole scene without footage through the Modify mode, or pixel-exact untouched regions.

name: Luma Ray3.14
summary: Native 1080p creation and rapid visual iteration.
specs: Text/image generation • Native 1080p • Modify workflow
strengths: A useful option for detailed B-roll, image animation and visual experiments.
weaknesses: This release does not provide every original Ray3 feature: character references and HDR/EXR Modify are limited/absent.
best: A textured food macro, scenic commercial shot or stylized visual metaphor.
worst: A workflow dependent on character-reference controls or native HDR Modify in this release.

name: MiniMax H3 / H3 Max
summary: Multimodal H3 plus a faster, narrower Max offering.
specs: H3: 4–15 seconds, 768P/2K • H3 Max: 5–15 seconds, 480P/768P
strengths: H3 combines video/audio/image references and editing; Max is an iteration choice for text/image generation.
weaknesses: Max is not simply higher resolution: its documented formats and reference support differ from H3.
best: Use H3 for reference-driven ads; Max for quick tests of a short shot.
worst: Choosing Max expecting every H3 reference/editing feature, or assuming both expose 2K.

name: Wan 3.0 / Prime
summary: An all-in-one generation family with a speed-oriented variant.
specs: 2–30 seconds • 480p/720p/1080p • Audio • Reference inputs
strengths: Longer short-form generation and integrated inputs suit connected scenes. Prime emphasizes speed.
weaknesses: Endpoint and region affect access; maximum duration does not guarantee continuity.
best: A short story with sound and reference material; Prime for iteration.
worst: Treating cloud Wan3 as downloadable Wan2.2 weights or relying on precise long-shot physics.

name: HappyHorse 1.1 / 1.0 Edit
summary: Generation and a separately versioned editing endpoint.
specs: 1.1: text/image/reference generation • 1.0: video editing
strengths: The family spans reference-led creation and footage transformation.
weaknesses: Do not assume 1.1 generation and 1.0 editing share identical controls. Provider versions differ.
best: A short reference-guided sequence; choose the Edit endpoint for existing footage.
worst: Selecting a generation endpoint expecting source-preserving video edits.

name: Wan 2.7
summary: A broad collection of creation and transformation modes.
specs: Text/image generation • Reference, first/last frame, continuation and editing
strengths: Task-specific endpoints support bridges between frames, continuation and footage-guided effects.
weaknesses: Duration and resolution differ by task; a single family name hides several interfaces.
best: Bridge approved start/end compositions or transform a source video's movement and appearance.
worst: Assuming every mode has identical duration, audio or reference limits.

name: Wan 2.6 / Flash
summary: Short-form generation with budget-conscious variants.
specs: Text/image workflows • Audio options depend on endpoint
strengths: Useful when an existing integration or faster variant meets the shot's needs.
weaknesses: Older generation and mode-dependent controls; compare cost per usable clip, including retries.
best: Simple product motion, background loops and drafts through an established integration.
worst: Complex multi-character storytelling chosen solely for nominal per-generation cost.

name: FLUX.3 Video
summary: Short audiovisual storytelling across visual styles.
specs: Up to 20 seconds • Native 720p, 1080p upscaled • Audio
strengths: Multilingual sound and flexible styling support ads, illustration and narrative shorts.
weaknesses: Upscaled 1080p is not native detail; launch roadmap features should not be assumed available.
best: An illustrated campaign brought to life or a stylized short with dialogue.
worst: Assuming open weights or video/audio reference controls are shipped because they were announced.

name: Vidu Q3
summary: Reference-guided animation and short audiovisual scenes.
specs: Up to 16 seconds • Audio/video • Reference workflows
strengths: Character assets and reference-based production are useful for recurring subjects and animation.
weaknesses: Complex scene consistency still needs review. The current homepage mixes generations and features.
best: A recurring animated character in short episodic scenes or product angles.
worst: Treating every homepage demonstration as Q3 output or expecting effortless feature-length continuity.

name: PixVerse V6 / C1
summary: General short-form creation plus a film-oriented C1 model.
specs: Up to 15 seconds • Up to 1080p • Audio
strengths: V6 serves broad creator workflows; C1 emphasizes action, effects and storyboard-led filmmaking.
weaknesses: Vendor demos are curated. Fast spectacle can obscure failures in contact, anatomy and spatial logic.
best: V6 for social shorts; C1 for an action concept or effects-heavy storyboard shot.
worst: An exact fight choreography with guaranteed contacts, or treating effects as proof of realism.

name: Pika 2.5 / Pikaffects
summary: Accessible short clips and playful transformations.
specs: Image animation • Effect templates • Capabilities vary by feature
strengths: Preset transformations are easy to art-direct for a simple visual gag.
weaknesses: Pikaffects is a product workflow, not a synonym for the base model; templates constrain outcomes.
best: A surreal product reveal, melting object or playful social post.
worst: Subtle long-form dramatic acting, exact scientific simulation or unrestricted professional compositing.

name: Midjourney Video
summary: Animate a strong starting image with minimal setup.
specs: 5-second clips • Extend up to 21 seconds • Manual/automatic motion
strengths: Fits image-first creators who already have a carefully art-directed still.
weaknesses: Extension can drift; it is an image-animation workflow, not a complete audio or editorial pipeline.
best: Animate an illustration, fashion image or atmospheric concept scene.
worst: Dialogue-first films, exact motion paths or preserving every detail through repeated extensions.

name: Grok Imagine Video 1.5
summary: API-oriented generation with improved native resolution.
specs: Native 1080p available • Text/image/reference workflows • Voice presets
strengths: A convenient option for integrating short audiovisual generation into applications.
weaknesses: Input and resolution choices affect cost; older launch demos do not establish current model quality.
best: Prototype a creative app or generate short scenes with a consistent preset voice.
worst: Assuming a generic model benchmark guarantees your exact identity, text or sound requirements.

name: Adobe Firefly Video / Video 2 Preview
summary: Creation and editing within an established creative ecosystem.
specs: Generation • Video 2 Preview editing • Transparent-background workflow
strengths: Camera controls, compositing features and Adobe integration suit post-production. Adobe describes licensed training inputs.
weaknesses: Preview and partner-model features are distinct; a training-policy claim is not a guarantee for every generated output.
best: Simple B-roll, compositing elements or a shot that will be finished in Adobe tools.
worst: Dense action with many interacting subjects, or assuming every Firefly-hosted model is Adobe's model.

name: Marey
summary: A production-focused option with explicit camera direction.
specs: Filmmaking controls • Vendor-described licensed training footage
strengths: Well matched to teams that value shot control and documented training provenance.
weaknesses: Access, workflow and economics require evaluation; licensed training alone does not settle all output-use questions.
best: A controlled commercial shot developed with a production team.
worst: Choosing solely for a 'safe' label or expecting an effortless low-cost viral-effects workflow.

name: LTX-2.5
summary: An adaptable audiovisual foundation with production formats.
specs: 22B parameters • Open weights • Native 4K/HDR/RAW capabilities
strengths: Self-hosting and adaptation offer control; multi-shot and audio support broaden production uses.
weaknesses: Large hardware demands. License terms vary with company revenue; vendor speed demos use high-end hardware.
best: A studio building a customized pipeline with capable GPUs and engineering support.
worst: A laptop-only deployment, assuming unrestricted licensing, or expecting benchmark hardware speed at home.

name: LTX-2.3
summary: An established controllable audiovisual pipeline.
specs: Portrait support • Audio • Pose/depth/edge controls • Fast/Pro options
strengths: Existing tooling and structural controls support repeatable, reference-led production.
weaknesses: Earlier model; speed, duration and quality differ by service tier and configuration.
best: A pipeline already tuned around LTX controls or portrait-oriented production.
worst: Assuming all LTX endpoints share the same limits or moving versions without evaluating compatibility.

name: Wan 2.2 / Animate
summary: Local generation and motion-transfer components.
specs: 5B and larger variants • Text/image generation • Animate specialist
strengths: Downloadable models enable custom deployment and adaptation; smaller variants lower the hardware barrier.
weaknesses: Core generation is not the same as Wan3 cloud audiovisual models. GPU, setup and finishing are your responsibility.
best: Self-hosted experimentation, fine-tuning or motion transfer with the Animate variant.
worst: A turnkey audio/video service with zero engineering or equating parameter size with quality.

name: HunyuanVideo 1.5
summary: A compact research and customization foundation.
specs: 8.3B parameters • Native 480p/720p • 1080p super-resolution
strengths: Documented offloading can lower GPU memory needs; useful for custom local pipelines.
weaknesses: Minimum-memory operation trades convenience and speed; core model does not supply a complete audio workflow.
best: A technically supported team fine-tuning visual style or experimenting locally.
worst: Instant consumer-laptop generation or calling super-resolution native 1080p.

name: Mochi 1
summary: An open research model focused on motion and prompt following.
specs: 480p preview • Apache 2.0 release
strengths: Accessible weights and code are useful for research, adaptation and understanding video generation.
weaknesses: Older low-resolution baseline; requires compute and does not match a modern integrated sound workflow.
best: Research experiments or a pipeline built around its existing weights.
worst: Selecting it by default for polished modern commercial delivery without substantial finishing.

name: CogVideoX / CogVideoX1.5
summary: A documented open video research family.
specs: Text/image variants • Local deployment • Variant-specific licensing
strengths: Useful research code and adaptation ecosystem for experiments and reproducible configurations.
weaknesses: Quality, memory and licensing vary by checkpoint; older families need more technical finishing.
best: Fine-tuning experiments and controlled comparisons with an existing CogVideo pipeline.
worst: A no-setup consumer workflow or assuming every checkpoint has the same commercial terms.

name: Stable Video Diffusion 1.1
summary: A short image-motion baseline retained for local workflows.
specs: Image-to-video • Hosted API deprecated July 24, 2025
strengths: Can remain useful in established local pipelines for subtle motion from a still.
weaknesses: Short silent output and older controls; the discontinued hosted API is not a new integration choice.
best: Animate a simple image within a pipeline already supporting the weights.
worst: New development dependent on Stability's former SVD API or complex directed storytelling.

name: Sora 2 / Sora 2 Pro
summary: A retiring audiovisual family, relevant chiefly to existing users.
specs: Web/app ended April 26, 2026 • API shutdown announced for September 24, 2026
strengths: Existing API users can complete supported short audiovisual experiments while access remains.
weaknesses: Near-term retirement dominates selection. Pro and base differ in quality/output options.
best: Finishing or migrating an existing workflow before the announced shutdown.
worst: Any new long-lived application or workflow that depends on continued availability.

name: HeyGen Avatar V / IV
summary: Presenter identity and talking-character production.
specs: Avatar V: video-based identity • Avatar IV: photo/stylized characters
strengths: A focused choice for repeatable presenters, localization and character speech.
weaknesses: Avatar workflows constrain scene freedom; naturalness still depends on input, voice and script.
best: V for a recurring spokesperson; IV for a photo-based or stylized talking character.
worst: Complex cinematic action, moving crowd scenes or a general-purpose environment generator.

name: Synthesia Expressive Avatars
summary: A structured presenter-video system for organizations.
specs: Avatar product family • Script-led video and localization
strengths: Templates and consistent presenters suit repeatable educational content.
weaknesses: A product workflow rather than a directly comparable open scene-generation model; performances can feel constrained.
best: Training, onboarding and multilingual explanations with a presenter.
worst: Cinematic action, unconventional character choreography or freeform world generation.

name: Hedra Avatar / Character-3 / Omnia
summary: Expressive characters, talking portraits and short full-body scenes.
specs: Audio-driven character workflows • Omnia emphasizes full-body/camera action
strengths: Voice-led characters work well for personality, song and expressive delivery.
weaknesses: Gestures may overshoot subtle acting; duration and output limits differ across current and legacy endpoints.
best: Avatar/Character-3 for a talking or singing character; Omnia for a short moving-character scene.
worst: Assuming long avatar duration also applies to Omnia, or subtle dramatic acting without iteration.
